units.title: Expenses
units.intro: Grammar: modals for inference about the future and the present (will be, might be, should be) and adverbial phrases and clauses.

lessons.title: Modals of inference: will, should, might

cards.title: Modals of inference: will, should, might
rule: **will (be)** = very sure: *Prices **will be** higher next year.* **should (be)** = expected / probable: *The loan **should be** approved by Friday.* **might / may (be)** = possible: *We **might** need extra money.*
**won’t** = sure it will not happen; **might not** = possibly not.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: One of the most challenging obstacles facing high school graduates ________ the rising cost of higher education.

steps.text: The subject of the sentence is 'One' (singular) in the pattern $$\text{One of} + \text{Plural Noun} + \text{Singular Verb}$$.
The plural noun phrase 'the most challenging obstacles' is part of a prepositional phrase modifying the subject.
Students often match the verb to the plural noun 'obstacles' which is closest to the verb slot, leading them to choose 'are' (Option A).

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The board of directors, despite having conflicting opinions on the new expansion policy, ________ finally agreed on the budget.

steps.text: The subject is 'The board' (singular collective noun).
The phrase 'of directors' and the parenthetical clause 'despite having conflicting opinions...' are intervening elements that do not change the subject's singular number.
Students are often distracted by the plural nouns 'directors' and 'opinions' and select the plural auxiliary 'have' (Option B).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Neither the regional program coordinator nor the senior researchers ________ present at the emergency project meeting yesterday.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
The compound subject is connected by the correlative conjunction 'Neither... nor'. The proximity rule applies, meaning the verb agrees with the closer subject, 'the senior researchers' (plural).

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Students may focus on 'the coordinator' (singular) and choose 'was' (Option A). The past time marker 'yesterday' eliminates present auxiliaries 'is' and 'are', leaving 'were' (Option B) as the correct choice.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
ምሉእ ሓሳብ ብ 'Neither... nor' ክእሰር ከሎ፡ እቲ ግሲ ምስቲ ናብኡ ዝቐረበ ባእታ ይሰማማዕ (Proximity Rule)። እቲ ዝቐረበ ባእታ 'the senior researchers' (ብዙሕ) ስለ ዝኾነን እቲ ግዜ ድማ 'yesterday' (ትማሊ) ስለ ዝኾነን፡ ቅኑዕ መልሲ 'were' (Option B) እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The local police ________ currently searching the forest area for the prisoners who escaped from the regional jail.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
'Police' is a collective noun that is always plural in English and must be paired with plural verbs.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Because 'police' does not end in '-s', students often assume it is singular and choose 'is' (Option A) or 'was' (Option C). The time marker 'currently' indicates present tense, which makes 'are' (Option B) correct.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Police' (ፖሊስ) ዝብል ስም ብቅርጹ ነጸላ ይመስል እምበር፡ ብሰዋስው ወግዒ ግን ወትሩ ብዙሕ ቁጽሪ (plural) እዩ። 'currently' (ኣብዚ እዋን) ዝብል ቃል ድማ ህልው እዋን ስለ ዝሕብር፡ ምስኡ ዝኸይድ ግሲ 'are' (Option B) እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: "Where's Ruth?" "She ____ be in the library; she usually studies there after class, but I'm not sure."
cards.why:
**Step 1:** The speaker says "I'm not sure".

**Step 2:** might expresses possibility.

**Step 3:** must and will are too certain; can't means impossible.

**Tip:** will = confident prediction, should = expected/probable, might = possible. Adverbial clauses answer when? why? how? where? or under what condition?

cards.title: Adverbial phrases and clauses
rule: An **adverbial** tells how, when, where, why or on what condition. A **phrase** has no subject + verb (*in the morning, to save money*). A **clause** has one (*because prices rose, so that we can save, although she earns a lot*).

Purpose: **so that / in order to / to**; negative purpose: **so as not to / lest** (formal, + should or base verb): *Save money **lest** you **(should) fall** into debt.* Contrast: **although / even though**.

examples.text: She saves money in order to buy a house.
Although he earns little but he saves.
examples.fix: Although he earns little, he saves.

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "Although he earns little but he saves."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** An **adverbial** tells how, when, where, why or on what condition. A **phrase** has no subject + verb (*in the morning, to save money*). A **clause** has one (*because prices rose, so that we can save, although she earns a lot*).
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "Although he earns little but he saves." breaks this rule.
**Step 3: Correct it.** "Although he earns little, he saves."

**Check:** Purpose: **so that / in order to / to**; negative purpose: **so as not to / lest** (formal, + should or base verb): *Save money **lest** you **(should) fall** into debt.* Contrast: **although / even though**.

cards.answer: Although he earns little, he saves.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Will = very sure, should = expected, might/may = possible, all + base verb. Adverbial phrases and clauses add time, reason, purpose (so that, in order to), negative purpose (lest, so as not to) and contrast (although).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: People continue to smoke____________ they know the danger.
cards.why: The sentence shows a contrast between an action and knowledge. 'Even though' introduces a clause of contrast (concession).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: _______________ having very little money, they are happy.
cards.why: 'In spite of' is followed by a gerund ('having'). 'Although' and 'Though' must be followed by a clause (Subject + Verb).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which sentence contains an adverbial clause of reason?

options.A: We stayed inside because it was raining.

cards.why:
**Step 1:** Reason answers "why?".

**Step 2:** "because it was raining" explains why we stayed inside.

**Step 3:** The others show time, place and manner.

**Tip:** will = confident prediction, should = expected/probable, might = possible. Adverbial clauses answer when? why? how? where? or under what condition?

glossary.meaning: A clause that acts like an adverb (when, because, although, so that...).
For fear that; introduces negative purpose.
